page: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v7 is an ARM-based cloud virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv7 server family, managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile supplies 96 dedicated arm64 virtual processors and 192 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 ratio of 2 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not incorporate graphics acceleration, offering zero GPUs. For storage, it integrates 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD disk capacity and maintains compatibility with premium storage configurations. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

The ARM64 architecture provides high dedicated core density while maintaining a lower memory allocation relative to standard general-purpose offerings. The local NVMe SSD subsystem delivers substantial high-speed temporary storage directly attached to the host, facilitating operations that require fast local scratch space or ephemeral data buffering. Because the instance provides 2 GB of RAM per vCPU, applications requiring extensive in-memory working sets may encounter constraints, shifting the architectural advantage toward compute-centric workloads with minimal per-thread memory footprints.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the reduced memory allocation per vCPU provides an efficient profile for multithreaded processing tasks that do not justify the cost of higher memory tiers. Microsoft Azure D96plds_v7 is suited for distributed software build and compilation environments, large CI/CD pipelines, batch processing jobs, video encoding, high-concurrency web serving clusters, and scale-out workloads relying on fast local NVMe file systems.
description: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine configuration within the Dpldsv7 series, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The server features 96 dedicated arm64 vCPUs paired with 192 GB of total system memory, establishing a 2 GB per core allocation suited for compute-oriented tasks rather than memory-heavy footprints. Storage capabilities include an integrated 5669 GB local NVMe SSD array along with support for premium remote storage, while hardware graphics acceleration is omitted with zero GPUs. Operating with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the configuration prioritizes high thread concurrency and local I/O throughput. The reduced memory-to-core ratio allows organizations to execute large-scale multithreaded processing with high resource density. Microsoft Azure D96plds_v7 fits workloads requiring extensive parallel computation and fast temporary scratch disks, such as distributed compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch analytics, video transcoding, and compute-focused web tier hosting.
